subject: Post-discovery: request for representative prompts and redaction guidance
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@olivetech.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@olivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-discovery: request for representative prompts and redaction guidance

Hi Priya / Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and an ask to keep our eval moving: 

Summary from our side:
- Goal: qualify model fit for Olive Tech’s AI-powered support summaries (short conversational transcripts -> concise multi-line summary + follow-up questions).
- Important constraints: strict PII redaction (name, SSN, account numbers), high recall on critical factual items, and sub-200ms median token latency for the async service.

Model recommendations (initial):
- Redwood-Opt-7B (fp16) — strong latency/cost tradeoff for conversation summarization.
- Llama2-13B-32k (quantized) — for higher-fidelity edge cases where recall matters.

What we need from Olive Tech to build a representative eval:
1) 100–200 representative prompt examples (actual user transcripts or synthetic prompts that mimic edge cases). Please include: customer message,-agent reply, and the expected summary (if available).
2) A short list of edge-case scenarios you worry most about (e.g., PII inside attachments, multi-party threads, truncated messages).
3) Your internal redaction policy or examples of what must be removed vs allowed (we attached a redaction template to make this simple).

I attached: prompt_sample_template.csv (CSV with columns: transcript, agent_response, expected_summary, sensitivity_flags) and a draft redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf — use either or send your own export.

Next steps / deadlines:
- If you can share a first batch by EOD Tues (2026-11-24) we’ll run an initial pass and return benchmark links and a small model comparison within 3 business days.
- We’ll also create a canary prompt set to monitor regression during rollout (Ben will own the canary design).

Open items for our team (internal): make sure we include lexicon-based redaction + model-based PII detection during evaluation.

Thanks — feel free to reply with the files directly or to drop them in the Drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: prompt_sample_template.csv, redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf
From: Priya Rao <priya@olivetech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@olivetech.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: request for representative prompts and redaction guidance

Thanks Mina — this looks great and aligns with our needs. A couple of quick clarifications before we export: 

1) For the "sensitivity_flags" column — can you confirm whether we should mark entity types (NAME, SSN, EMAIL) or provide free-text guidance?
2) We have some transcripts that include screenshots/attachments mentioned in the thread (no binary attached in the CSV). Should we include a short description like "screenshot contains account number" in a separate column?

We can get an initial 60–80 demo transcripts over by Wednesday EOD. We'll attach a small redaction spec (internal) — but we may need your team to validate the redaction approach on one sample first.

— Priya
Priya Rao
Head of Product, Olive Tech
priya@olivetech.com | +1 (628) 555-4499
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: request for representative prompts and redaction guidance (internal)

Mina — quick internal note before we ship the template to Olive: 

- Recommend we ask for 10 explicit canary prompts that exercise hallucination risk (e.g., missing context, contradictory facts). We'll use these for nightly regression checks.
- Add a "redact_confirmed" boolean to the CSV for rows where Olive has already redacted content on their side so we can separate raw vs pre-redacted samples.
- I dropped a quick link (benchmarks_quicklink.txt) with our baseline numbers for the two recommended models across their expected sequence lengths — include that in the message to get alignment on SLOs.

I'll be available to join the validation session next week if needed.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attached: benchmarks_quicklink.txt
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@olivetech.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@olivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: request for representative prompts and redaction guidance

Priya / Samir — perfect, thanks for the quick reply and the plan. A few operational notes to keep things moving: 

- For sensitivity_flags: please mark entity types (NAME, SSN, EMAIL, ACCT_NUM) in the column; use "REDACTED" in the transcript column when you have already redacted. Anything you mark as raw we'll treat as sensitive and redact prior to storage.
- For attachments/screenshots: include a short text description in the new column "attachment_notes" — our evaluation harness supports that meta field.
- Timeline: first batch by 2026-11-24 EOD; Redwood will return an initial eval report (model comparison + sample canary pass) by 2026-11-29 COB.

Next meeting: I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Wed 2026-11-25 to walk the team through the template and redaction expectations — tentative invite to follow.

Thanks again — looking forward to the sample set.

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
